newsitem.title: KENYA: Witnesses say Kenyan 17-year-old shot by police.
newsitem.headline: Witnesses say Kenyan 17-year-old shot by police.

text.p: Witnesses said police shot and killed a 17-year-old youth on Monday in the town of Thika, one of four people killed in Kenya during a day of clashes.

They told Reuters David Mutugi, 17, was shot in the chest and killed by police at Moi gardens in Thika when police and prison guards violently dispersed people gathering for a demonstration by groups demanding constitutional reforms from the government of President Daniel arap Moi.
"Mutugi was running with two other guys and the police shot him in the chest and he fell," said witness Moses Gachamba.
Hospital sources said at least five other people were injured, most by beating, when police broke up a crowd in Moi gardens, which also has a large secondhand clothes market.
His 20-year-old sister, Lydia Nyawira, said the last time she saw her brother alive was on Monday morning when he went to the market to open up a kiosk which was run by his family.
His mother said she had gone to the town mortuary but was not allowed by officials to see the body of her son.
Police spokesman Assistant Commissioner Peter Kimanthi said it was unclear whether Mutugi was the same person as the body of a boy police said was brought to the road in the Majengo area of Thika.
He said an investigation was underway into the death but police had not been active in Majengo.
